formulation.rationale: All mapped products are U-100 insulin glargine products (Lantus, Basaglar, or Semglee/insulin glargine-yfgn). The compared perioperative society guidance addresses standard long-acting glargine without distinguishing these U-100 brands.

passages.locator: Table 2, Basal insulin (long-acting insulin analog: Glargine)
passages.quote: Reducing the dose 20%-30% starting the night before the procedure, with the following precaution: In patients receiving a high proportion of basal insulin (> 50% of total daily insulin), consider reducing the dose by up to 50%.

passages.locator: Table 2, Basal insulin (long-acting insulin analog: Glargine)
passages.quote: In patients on a basal–bolus regimen with < 50% of total daily insulin as basal, dose reduction may not be necessary. In such cases, maintaining the usual basal dose may minimize hyperglycemia and glycemic variability

comparisons.checked_locators: Table 2, Basal insulin (long-acting insulin analog: Glargine)
comparisons.note: The 2026 joint statement gives a glargine-specific night-before reduction with conditional larger reduction for high basal proportions and possible no reduction when basal is less than 50% of total daily insulin.

comparisons.checked_locators: Perioperative Care, insulin therapy adjustments; Insulin Therapy Recommendations 16.8 and 16.9
comparisons.note: ADA provides a current long-acting basal-insulin adjustment before surgery and retains basal insulin across NPO/poor-intake and adequate-intake states.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: USMSTF does not provide a glargine-specific dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication planning with the prescribing clinician.

recommendations.timing_text: Reducing the dose 20%-30% starting the night before the procedure
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.applicability: Elective procedure in a patient receiving standard long-acting insulin glargine.
recommendations.exceptions: For basal insulin exceeding 50% of total daily insulin, the same passage permits reduction up to 50%.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian joint statement recommends reducing standard glargine by 20%-30% starting the night before the procedure.

recommendations.qualifier: basal-bolus regimen with basal under 50% of total daily insulin
recommendations.timing_text: dose reduction may not be necessary
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.applicability: Glargine used in a basal-bolus regimen where basal is less than 50% of total daily insulin.
recommendations.summary: When basal insulin is less than 50% of total daily insulin, the Brazilian joint statement says glargine dose reduction may not be necessary.

recommendations.timing_text: On the evening before surgery, reduce long-acting basal insulin analogs to 75–80% of the usual dose
recommendations.strength: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.certainty: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.applicability: Long-acting basal insulin analogue use before surgery, including glargine U-100.
recommendations.exceptions: ADA states that adjustment depends on diabetes type and clinical judgment.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends reducing long-acting basal insulin analogues to 75–80% of the usual dose on the evening before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or taking nothing by mouth.
recommendations.exceptions: This establishes continuation of a basal component but does not specify a product-specific glargine U-100 dose.
recommendations.summary: ADA retains basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan during poor oral intake or NPO status.

recommendations.qualifier: postprocedure poor oral intake or NPO
recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with poor oral intake or still NPO.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed glargine restart time is stated.
recommendations.summary: When oral intake remains poor or the patient remains NPO, ADA retains basal insulin in the preferred insulin plan.

recommendations.timing_text: an insulin plan with basal, prandial, and correction components is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with adequate nutritional intake.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed glargine restart time is stated.
recommendations.summary: With adequate nutritional intake, ADA includes basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan.

scenario_coverage.reason: SBD/SBA/ABESO and ADA both provide preprocedure basal-insulin dose adjustment frameworks.
ADA retains basal insulin during poor oral intake or NPO status.
ADA includes basal insulin in preferred regimens for both poor/NPO and adequate nutritional intake states.

conflicts.description: SBD/SBA/ABESO recommends a 20%-30% glargine reduction starting the night before the procedure with conditional alternatives based on basal proportion, whereas ADA recommends 75–80% of the usual long-acting basal dose on the evening before surgery. The frameworks overlap but are not identical and are preserved separately.

open_questions.text: USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific U-100 glargine dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic management with the prescribing clinician.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package for U-100 glargine only. U-300 glargine was split because current society guidance treats its prolonged pharmacokinetics differently.
